evidence: createApp: route handlers only call catalogue.* and orders.* application services and serialize results with res.json
statusFor/errorHandler: map DomainError subclasses to HTTP status codes (400/404/409/500), a transport concern
param/asObject/requireString/requireNumber: check the shape and type of request input only, with no business invariants
POST /orders/:id/pay|pack|ship|deliver pass a fixed target state to orders.transition, and transition validity stays in the lower layers
GET /stock only reshapes listProducts() output into a response format and computes nothing new
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/http.ts is an HTTP adapter. Its jobs are to set up the Express app and routes, pass requests to the application services (CatalogueService, OrderService), check the shape of incoming data, and turn domain errors into HTTP status codes and JSON bodies. All of these are transport concerns that belong in infrastructure. The file has no business rules of its own. Inventory and reservation logic and state-transition rules are left to orders.transition, orders.advance, orders.cancel and catalogue.restock. The shortcut routes (/pay, /pack, /ship, /deliver) only pick a fixed target state and pass it on, and the domain layer still decides whether that transition is allowed. The /stock handler only reshapes data for the response. The isOrderState check uses the domain's own predicate to validate input and does not restate the rule. It does no persistence work.
